transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Am I... is this chair okay? Okay, thank you. 

Um, well, I hope I'm not overreacting, because it's probably just stress. I run a company, so things get pretty intense, as I'm sure you can imagine. But I wanted to make sure I was doing the right thing by getting it checked out. 

I've been... well, it's a little embarrassing to admit, but I keep hearing people talking about me. Like, through the conference room walls at work, or even from my phone when it's completely turned off. It's usually the board members or my staff, and they're saying that I'm ruining the company. It's just... it sounds so real and so clear that I actually answer them back out loud before I realize that no one else in the room heard it. 

I know that probably sounds terrible, and I'm really hoping it's just exhaustion, but... does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm in the right place for this.
When you hear these voices talking about you, do you believe at that moment that they are actually real people speaking, or do you know right away that it's not real?

Well, um... at the exact moment it happens, I... I really do think it's them. I hope that doesn't make me sound completely crazy. 

It's just that they sound so incredibly clear. Like I was saying, I'll hear the board members or my staff criticizing me through the walls, and the voices are so distinct and so real that I literally just answer them back. I'll defend myself right out loud without even thinking about it. It's only a few seconds later, when I realize my phone is actually completely turned off, or I notice that no one else in the room reacted at all, that I catch myself and realize they aren't really there. 

So, yes, in that split second, I completely believe they are real people speaking to me. I know I shouldn't, and I try really hard to catch it faster now so I don't embarrass myself... am I making sense? I just really hope it's a normal reaction to being overworked.

Over the past few weeks or months, have you been experiencing any significant changes in your mood—like feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or conversely, unusually energetic or euphoric—separate from the stress about the voices?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I definitely haven't been feeling depressed or hopeless. I try really hard to keep a positive attitude, especially for my team, you know? 

And I haven't been unusually energetic or anything like that either. Just... just my normal self, really, aside from the stress of... well, everything I just mentioned with the voices. I really think my mood has been completely fine. 

Is... is that a good thing? I hope that's helpful for you to know. I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information so we can figure this out.
How long have you been experiencing these voices? Did they start suddenly over a few days, or have they been building up over weeks or months?

Um... well, it hasn't been forever or anything like that. I've been trying to keep track, just to be thorough... and I think the voices, you know, the ones from the walls or my phone, they've been happening for about the past three months. 

It wasn't like a sudden, crazy snap or anything. I don't want you to think I just woke up one day and lost my mind. It was more... gradual, I guess? Just building up slowly while work was getting more and more stressful. 

Three months isn't that long in the grand scheme of things, right? I mean, I'm hoping since it hasn't been happening for years, it'll be easier to fix. Does that timeline make sense for someone who's just dealing with a lot of executive burnout?

Over these past three months with the voices, have there been any stretches of time—days or weeks—where you didn't hear them at all and everything felt completely normal, or have they been happening fairly consistently throughout?

Well, um... I guess they've been pretty consistent? I mean, I try really hard not to let it bother me, but... no, there really haven't been any long breaks. It's not like they go away for weeks at a time. 

I really wish I could say they did. I know it probably sounds bad that it's happening so often, but it's just... it's just been a steady thing, almost every day. I hope that doesn't make my case too difficult to manage? I promise I'm still functioning really well at work despite it all. I just want to be completely honest with you so you know exactly what we're dealing with. Is that... is that the kind of pattern you usually see with severe stress?

Before these voices started three months ago, did you notice any changes in yourself—like difficulty concentrating, withdrawing from friends or activities, or feeling like something was 'off'—even if you didn't hear voices yet?

Um... well... I guess if I'm being completely honest—and I do want to be a good patient and give you the full picture—maybe things have felt a little... off... for longer than three months. 

I really didn't want to bring it up because I don't want you to think I've been falling apart for years, because I haven't! I've been doing a great job at work. But... well, I suppose it's been building for about two years and four months. That's when the company expansion happened and they put me in charge of the new arts-and-commerce division. 

It was just such a huge promotion, and I wanted to be perfect, you know? So I started working late, skipping lunches, maybe not seeing my friends as much... but that's just what dedicated executives do, right? It's totally normal to get a little withdrawn when you're focusing on a big career move. I just... I hope you don't think less of me for letting the stress build up for that long. It really just started as me trying to be the best leader I could be. Does that make sense?

During these past two years, have there been any periods where you felt like you needed significantly less sleep than usual—like sleeping only 3-4 hours but still feeling completely rested and energized—or times when your thoughts were racing so fast you could barely keep up with them?

Um, no, definitely not. I mean, I'm a good sleeper, usually. I know sleep is super important for, you know, cognitive function and being an effective executive. 

I definitely don't have that thing where I only sleep a few hours and feel amazing. I wish I did, honestly, it would make getting through all my emails a lot easier! But no, I usually try to get my full eight hours. Sometimes I might toss and turn a bit if I'm worrying about a big presentation, but I definitely feel tired if I don't sleep. 

And my thoughts... I mean, I have a lot of thoughts because I have a lot of responsibilities, but they aren't racing out of control or anything. I'm very organized. I keep lists and schedules to make sure everything stays on track. So, no, I haven't had anything like that. That's a good thing, right? That means I'm just dealing with regular stress and not something more serious?

Before the voices started three months ago, did you ever feel like people were watching you, or that things around you had special meanings directed at you, or notice yourself doing things very differently than you normally would—even without hearing voices?

Um... well... I guess there have been a few... little things. Nothing major, I promise! I just... I really want to be helpful and give you the right answers. 

As for people watching me or special meanings, no, not really. I'm just a normal executive trying to do a good job. But... well, you asked about doing things differently, and... I suppose I have had a few... awkward moments? 

I feel so silly even mentioning it, because I know it sounds unprofessional, and I really pride myself on being professional. But sometimes, in meetings or at our gallery events, I'll just... I don't know, I'll suddenly stand up. And I might start rearranging the pens on the table, or the name cards, putting them into these specific patterns. Or... or I might repeat a phrase someone just said, out loud. Sometimes I even hold my hands up in the air, like I'm presenting something, but... but there's nothing there. 

Afterward, I always realize it made absolutely no sense for the room, and I feel so embarrassed. I try to play it off like I was just stretching or organizing, because I don't want my team to think their CEO is acting strangely. It's just a little quirk from being so overwhelmed with the arts-and-commerce division, right? Like my brain just needs a physical outlet for a second? I really hope that doesn't sound too strange to you. I'm trying so hard to keep everything running smoothly.

Over these past two years, have you noticed that you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy doing, or that it feels harder to get motivated to do activities outside of work—even things you used to find fun or meaningful?

Um... well... it’s a little hard to admit this, because I really pride myself on being a go-getter. I want you to know I've always been incredibly dedicated. But... if I'm being completely honest with you, and I do want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information... I guess things have changed a bit. 

I used to be the person driving every single idea. After our gallery openings, I’d be the one calling everyone, so excited, just buzzing with energy to talk about how it went. But for a while now... I just... 

I'll sit at my desk for hours, just staring at the agenda. Not even reading it, really, just staring at it. And I barely speak to my staff anymore. Or... or even my husband when I get home. I just kind of sit there. And the worst part, the part I feel so guilty about, is that I feel almost nothing about the work I used to absolutely love. It's like the volume on my feelings just got turned all the way down. 

I really hope you don't think I'm just being lazy or that I'm a bad wife or a bad CEO. I promise I'm not trying to slack off! It’s just... it's normal to get a little burnt out and quiet when you've been pushing so hard for so long, isn't it? A lot of successful people go through phases where they just need to detach for a bit, right?

When you're sitting at your desk staring at the agenda, or when you're home with your husband not speaking—do you feel like you want to engage but just can't find the energy, or is it more that you don't really feel like talking to anyone at all, like the desire itself has gone away?

Um... well... I guess... I think it's more that the desire is just... gone. Which sounds terrible, I know. I really don't want you to think I'm cold or that I don't care about my husband or my team. I do care! I've always been such a dedicated person. 

But... yeah, when I'm just sitting there staring at the agenda for hours, or when I'm quiet at home... it's not like I'm sitting there wishing I could talk and just feeling too tired. It's more like... I just don't feel the need to. Like I said, I used to be the one driving every idea, calling everyone after the gallery openings because I was so excited. But now... I just feel almost nothing about the work I used to love. And I barely speak to my husband or my staff because I just... I don't really want to talk. 

I feel so awful admitting that. It sounds so unprofessional and... and unloving. But it's just a phase, right? Like, a normal reaction to being a CEO and handling so much pressure for so long? I'm sure it's just a temporary thing and I'll bounce back to being my usual, energetic self soon. That makes sense, doesn't it?

Right now, when you hear these voices—even though you've learned they're not real—do you still have moments where part of you believes they might actually be real, or do you now know for certain they aren't real even while you're hearing them?

Um... well... I want to give you the right answer, because I know we talked about how they aren't real, and I really am trying to understand that. I promise I am listening to everything you tell me. 

But... if I'm being completely honest—and I know I need to be honest so you can help me—it's... it's still really hard sometimes. Because they sound so incredibly clear. 

Like... when I'm in my office, I'll hear them talking about me through the conference room walls, or... or even coming from my phone when it's completely turned off. It sounds exactly like the board members, or my staff, and they're... they're saying these awful things, saying I'm ruining the company. And in those moments, it sounds so real that I'll actually answer them out loud. I'll try to defend myself before I even realize that no one else in the room heard it. 

I feel so foolish when I catch myself doing it. I know I'm supposed to know they aren't real now, and I really am trying to keep that in mind! But in the split second when I hear them... my brain just reacts like they're actually there. Does that make sense? I hope you don't think I'm failing at this or not trying hard enough to ignore them. It's just... they're very convincing sometimes, you know?

When you hear these voices saying you're ruining the company, and you answer them out loud—afterward, when you realize no one else heard them, do you think to yourself 'that wasn't real, my mind created that,' or do you find yourself wondering 'maybe they really were talking about me, but somehow no one else noticed'?

Um... well, it's... I really want to be doing this right, you know? I want to make sure I'm thinking about it the way you want me to. 

When I catch myself talking back, and I see that no one else is reacting... I... I do try to tell myself what we talked about. I really do. I try to say, "Okay, that's just my mind playing tricks on me." Because I know that's the right answer, and I really want to be a good patient and get a handle on this. 

But... oh, this is so embarrassing to admit... sometimes, just for a little bit, I do wonder. I think... maybe they *were* talking about me. Maybe they're just being really quiet, or maybe they have some sort of earpiece, or... or maybe they're just ignoring me on purpose to make me feel crazy. 

I know I shouldn't think that! I know I'm supposed to just know it's not real. Please don't be disappointed in me. I promise I'm working really hard to remind myself that it's just my brain. It's just... when you're under so much pressure at work, it's natural to feel a little paranoid about what people are saying behind your back, right? That's a pretty normal thing for a CEO to worry about, isn't it?

Right now, in this moment as we're talking, if you heard one of those voices again, would you be able to recognize it as not real before you responded to it, or would you still feel pulled to believe it was actually someone talking to you?

Um... well... I want to say yes. I really want to say that I would recognize it immediately. I know that's what we've been working toward, and I promise I've been trying so hard to apply what you've been teaching me. 

But... if it happened right now... I think I'd still feel pulled to believe it. Like I mentioned before, when I hear them—the board members or my staff—coming through the conference room walls or even my phone when it's completely off... they just sound so incredibly real. They're saying those awful things about how I'm ruining the company, and it's just so clear. 

I'm so sorry, I know I shouldn't be reacting to them anymore. But in that split second, the pull is just so strong. I usually end up answering them out loud before my brain even catches up to realize that no one else in the room heard a thing. 

I feel terrible admitting that. I really want to be doing better for you. I'm trying my best, I promise. It's just... it's a lot harder to ignore than I thought it would be. Is it normal that it takes this long to get the hang of it? I really hope you don't think I'm not trying.

When you hear those voices right now, and you know intellectually that they aren't real—do you still feel, deep down, like there's a real possibility they might actually be people trying to communicate with you, or are you completely certain in your heart that they're just something your mind is producing?

I... I really want to tell you that I'm one hundred percent certain it's just my mind. I know that's the right answer, and I'm trying so hard to get there, I really am. 

But... deep down... oh, I feel so silly admitting this because I know I keep repeating myself... but when it happens, it just feels so intentional. Like when I hear the board members or my staff through the conference room walls, or... or from my phone when I know for a fact it's completely turned off... a part of me really does feel like they are actually there, trying to communicate with me. Or maybe test me? 

Because they're always saying I'm ruining the company, and it sounds so perfectly clear that, like I said, I just instinctively answer them out loud before I even realize no one else heard it. 

So... I guess in my heart, there's still that piece of me that believes it's really them. I'm so sorry, I know I'm supposed to be completely certain it's just my mind by now. I know that's what we've been working on. Please tell me I'm not failing at this. I am making some progress, aren't I?

When you're not in a moment where you're hearing the voices, and you have time to think clearly—like right now, sitting here with me—do you believe that these voices are definitely a symptom of an illness in your mind, or do you genuinely believe that real people are actually trying to communicate with you through the walls and your phone?

I... I know I'm probably frustrating you by going in circles, and I really don't mean to. I want to give you the right answer. I want to sit here and say, yes, absolutely, I know it's just a symptom of an illness. That's what a rational person should think, right? 

But... oh, it's just so embarrassing to admit this... even right now, when it's quiet and we're just talking... I can't completely shake it. Because my memory of it is just so vivid. When I think back to hearing the staff or the board members through the conference room walls, or... or coming through my phone when I know it's completely powered down... I can still remember the exact tone they use when they say I'm ruining the company. It's so clear that, like I said, I just instinctively answer them out loud before I even have a chance to realize no one else heard it. 

So... I guess, honestly... even when I'm thinking clearly, a part of me genuinely believes they really are finding some way to communicate with me. I'm so sorry. I know I'm supposed to know better by now, and I really am trying to look at it the way you do. Please tell me you're not giving up on me... I am trying, aren't I?

If I were to tell you right now that what you're experiencing—these voices and the belief that people are communicating with you through walls and your phone—is definitely caused by your brain producing these experiences, not by real people actually trying to reach you, would you be able to accept that as true, or do you genuinely believe that real people really are doing this to you?

I... I really want to say I accept it. I want to agree with you completely, because I know you're the expert and you're just trying to help me. I promise I value your opinion so much. 

But... oh, this is so hard to say without sounding like I'm ignoring you... I just... I still feel like they really are doing it. I know you're saying it's my brain, and I'm trying so hard to wrap my head around that, but... when I hear the board members or my staff coming through the conference room walls, or... or from my phone when it's completely off... it just doesn't feel like a brain thing. It feels like they are actually there, saying I'm ruining the company. It's so clear that I just... I answer them out loud before I even realize no one else heard it. 

I'm so sorry. I know I'm probably being such a difficult patient right now. I really don't want to be. I want to be doing this right. Is it okay that I still struggle with this? I promise I'll keep trying to see it your way, I really will.

Let me ask you this directly: Right now, sitting here with me, if you think about the board members or staff supposedly communicating through the walls or your turned-off phone—do you think it's actually possible that they're really doing that, or do you think your brain is creating those experiences even though they feel real?

I... I know you want me to say it's just my brain. And I really, really want to give you that answer, I do. I want to be a good patient and show you that I'm getting better. 

But... oh, I feel terrible saying this again... I still think it's possible they're really doing it. I know how crazy that sounds, and I'm so embarrassed to admit it. But when I hear them—the board members, my staff—talking about me through the conference room walls, or when my phone is completely turned off... it's just so real. They're saying I'm ruining the company, and it's so clear that I just... I answer them out loud. I don't even think about it, I just respond before I realize no one else is hearing it.

I'm sorry. I know that's not the right answer. I know I'm supposed to understand that it's my brain creating it. I am trying to get there, I promise. I'm not a hopeless case, am I? I really am trying to understand what you're telling me.
When you first started hearing these voices three months ago, did you immediately know they weren't real, or did it take you time to figure out that no one else was hearing them?

I... oh gosh, I want to give you a clear answer for this, I really do. I know timelines are important for you to figure everything out. But... I'm honestly not sure. 

I... I can't quite remember how it all started back then, or... or when exactly I noticed that no one else was reacting to them. It's all just a bit of a blur, I'm afraid. I'm so sorry, I feel like I should know this. Is it okay that I don't remember exactly? I hope I'm not messing up your notes by not having a better answer for you...

I want to be very clear about something. Right now, in this moment, do you truly believe that real people are actually communicating with you through those walls and your phone, or do you know for certain that your brain is creating these experiences even though they feel completely real?

I... I know you just asked me this, and I really want to give you the answer you're looking for. I want to say I know for certain it's just my brain. I know that's what I'm supposed to say, and I want to be doing this right. 

But... oh, please don't be upset with me... I still think it's really them. I know I'm probably frustrating you, and I'm so sorry. I just... I can't shake the feeling that they're really there, talking through the walls and the phone. It just feels too real. 

I'm sorry, I know that's the wrong answer again. I'm trying so hard to be a good patient, I really am. Am I doing okay, despite this? I promise I'll keep working on it.

doctor.intent: Establish rapport and identify the chief complaint that brings the patient to psychiatric evaluation
doctor.question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

target_item.name: Hallucinations
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I keep hearing people talking about me through the conference room walls or from my phone even when it’s off, usually board members or staff saying I’m ruining the company, and it sounds so clear that I answer them before I realize no one else heard it.
target_item.reason: This is the first reply of the consultation, so I must return the chief complaint symptom code S020.

patient.answer:
Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Am I... is this chair okay? Okay, thank you. 

Um, well, I hope I'm not overreacting, because it's probably just stress. I run a company, so things get pretty intense, as I'm sure you can imagine. But I wanted to make sure I was doing the right thing by getting it checked out. 

I've been... well, it's a little embarrassing to admit, but I keep hearing people talking about me. Like, through the conference room walls at work, or even from my phone when it's completely turned off. It's usually the board members or my staff, and they're saying that I'm ruining the company.
